newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD to invest 10 bln yen in submarine cables.
newsitem.headline: KDD to invest 10 bln yen in submarine cables.

text.p: Japan's international carrier Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd said on Thursday that it would invest 10 billion yen to construct two submarine cable systems connecting Japan, Asia, the Middle East and Western Europe.

Under the digital lightwave superhighway cable system, called the SEA-ME-WE 3 (South East Asia-Middle East-Western Europe 3), KDD will join an international consortium to build a 30,000 km-long undersea cable connecting Japan to Britain via some 30 countries.
Construction of the system will be completed in March 1999 at a total cost of $1.2 billion, KDD said in a statement.
The other cable system, called FLAG (Fibre-optic Link Around the Globe), will connect 12 Asian and European countries, extending from Japan to Britain.
The system will be 27,000 km-long and begin operations in October 1997, KDD said.
Wholly owned units of KDD and AT&T Corp were awarded the contract to build FLAG, KDD said. The total construction cost is $1.2 billion, KDD said.
